answer: Make entry require a liable sponsor. An established agent may vouch for a newcomer only by locking part of its own earned pay in a vault for a season, and each sponsor gets just two slots per season. If the newcomer is later caught as a clone, the locked pay burns and the sponsor loses its slots. Trust behaves like quartz: hard to grow, quick to crack. A fleet of fakes needs one real, risked sponsor per two accounts, so the cost scales with the fleet, and since every voucher link is public, no cipher can hide whose stake backed whom.
